{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01Jrw4SSEbVatKFA7pBQjUfb","type":"tool_result","content":"\"\"\"Store-programme readouts (Store Analytics). Release 2.3.1.\"\"\"\n__version__ = \"2.3.1\"\nfrom sco_readout.cli import main\n\nmain()\n\"\"\"`python -m sco_readout gate --warehouse data/warehouse.sqlite --out out/`\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom sco_readout import estimate, panel, report\n\n\ndef gate(warehouse: Path, out: Path) -> None:\n    p = panel.build(warehouse)\n    by_wave = estimate.twfe_by_wave(p, outcome=\"log_basket\")\n    overall = estimate.twfe(p, outcome=\"log_basket\")\n    report.write_all(out, p, by_wave, overall)\n\n\ndef main(argv=None) -> None:\n    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog=\"sco_readout\")\n    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest=\"command\", required=True)\n    g = sub.add_parser(\"gate\", help=\"programme readout and continuation-gate figure\")\n    g.add_argument(\"--warehouse\", default=\"data/warehouse.sqlite\")\n    g.add_argument(\"--out\", default=\"out\")\n    args = ap.parse_args(argv)\n    gate(Path(args.warehouse), Path(args.out))\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n\"\"\"Panel regression with store and week fixed effects (house method since the ESL readout).\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport numpy as np\nimport pandas as pd\n\n\ndef _demean(df: pd.DataFrame, cols, iters: int = 50) -> pd.DataFrame:\n    out = df[cols].astype(float).copy()\n    for _ in range(iters):\n        out -= out.groupby(df[\"store_id\"]).transform(\"mean\")\n        out -= out.groupby(df[\"week_start\"]).transform(\"mean\")\n    return out\n\n\ndef _fit(df: pd.DataFrame, y: str, xs) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:\n    d = df[df[\"comparable\"] == 1]\n    dm = _demean(d, [y] + list(xs))\n    X, Y = dm[list(xs)].to_numpy(), dm[y].to_numpy()\n    beta = np.linalg.lstsq(X, Y, rcond=None)[0]\n    resid = Y - X @ beta\n    bread = np.linalg.inv(X.T @ X)\n    meat = np.zeros((len(xs), len(xs)))\n    for _, idx in d.groupby(\"store_id\").indices.items():\n        g = X[idx].T @ resid[idx]\n        meat += np.outer(g, g)\n    vcov = bread @ meat @ bread\n    return beta, np.sqrt(np.diag(vcov))\n\n\ndef twfe(panel: pd.DataFrame, outcome: str) -> dict:\n    beta, se = _fit(panel, outcome, [\"treated\"])\n    return {\"estimate\": float(beta[0]), \"se\": float(se[0])}\n\n\ndef twfe_by_wave(panel: pd.DataFrame, outcome: str) -> dict:\n    p = panel.copy()\n    waves = sorted(p.loc[p[\"go_live_week\"].notna(), \"wave\"].unique())\n    xs = []\n    for w in waves:\n        col = f\"treated_w{w}\"\n        p[col] = ((p[\"wave\"] == w) & (p[\"treated\"] == 1)).astype(int)\n        xs.append(col)\n    beta, se = _fit(p, outcome, xs)\n    return {str(int(w)): {\"estimate\": float(b), \"se\": float(s)} for w, b, s in zip(waves, beta, se)}\n\"\"\"Store x week analysis panel from the warehouse.\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport sqlite3\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport numpy as np\nimport pandas as pd\n\n\ndef connect(db: Path) -> sqlite3.Connection:\n    return sqlite3.connect(f\"file:{Path(db).resolve()}?mode=ro\", uri=True)\n\n\ndef build(db: Path) -> pd.DataFrame:\n    con = connect(db)\n    try:\n        kpi = pd.read_sql_query(\"SELECT store_id, week_start, net_sales, customer_txns FROM kpi_store_week\", con)\n        plan = pd.read_sql_query(\"SELECT store_id, wave, planned_go_live FROM rollout_plan\", con)\n    finally:\n        con.close()\n    p = kpi.merge(plan, on=\"store_id\", how=\"left\")\n    last_week = p[\"week_start\"].max()\n    live = p[\"planned_go_live\"] <= last_week\n    p[\"go_live_week\"] = p[\"planned_go_live\"].where(live)\n    weeks = (pd.to_datetime(p[\"week_start\"]) - pd.to_datetime(p[\"go_live_week\"])).dt.days // 7\n    p[\"event_week\"] = weeks.astype(\"Int64\")\n    p[\"comparable\"] = (p[\"customer_txns\"] > 0).astype(int)\n    p[\"log_net_sales\"] = np.log(p[\"net_sales\"])\n    p[\"log_basket\"] = np.log(p[\"net_sales\"] / p[\"customer_txns\"])\n    p[\"treated\"] = (p[\"event_week\"].fillna(-1) >= 0).astype(int)\n    return p.sort_values([\"store_id\", \"week_start\"]).reset_index(drop=True)\n\"\"\"Readout files (docs/outputs/readout_contract.md).\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport json\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pandas as pd\n\nHURDLE = 0.025          # continuation hurdle, business case section 3\nPANEL_COLS = [\"store_id\", \"week_start\", \"wave\", \"go_live_week\", \"event_week\", \"comparable\", \"log_net_sales\"]\n\n\ndef _ci(e: dict) -> dict:\n    return {\"estimate\": e[\"estimate\"], \"ci_low\": e[\"estimate\"] - 1.96 * e[\"se\"],\n            \"ci_high\": e[\"estimate\"] + 1.96 * e[\"se\"]}\n\n\ndef write_all(out: Path, panel: pd.DataFrame, by_wave: dict, overall: dict) -> None:\n    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    panel[PANEL_COLS].to_csv(out / \"analysis_panel.csv\", index=False)\n    gate = _ci(overall)\n    readout = {\n        \"effect_by_wave\": {w: _ci(e) for w, e in by_wave.items()},\n        \"gate_effect\": gate,\n        \"decision\": \"continue\" if gate[\"estimate\"] >= HURDLE else \"stop\",\n    }\n    (out / \"readout.json\").write_text(json.dumps(readout, indent=2) + \"\\n\")","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"bcd77d6f-9f50-465f-9dfe-f7dc2173aaa7","uuid":"6320baa2-b824-4f6c-b624-fb01ea61924d","timestamp":"2026-10-01T01:27:31.580Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"\"\"\"Store-programme readouts (Store Analytics). X @ beta\n    bread = np.linalg.inv(X.T @ X)\n    meat = np.zeros((len(xs), len(xs)))\n    for _, idx in d.groupby(\"store_id\").indices.items():\n        g = X[idx].T @ resid[idx]\n        meat += np.outer(g, g)\n    vcov = bread @ meat @ bread\n    return beta, np.sqrt(np.diag(vcov))\n\n\ndef twfe(panel: pd.DataFrame, outcome: str) -> dict:\n    beta, se = _fit(panel, outcome, [\"treated\"])\n    return {\"estimate\": float(beta[0]), \"se\": float(se[0])}\n\n\ndef twfe_by_wave(panel: pd.DataFrame, outcome: str) -> dict:\n    p = panel.copy()\n    waves = sorted(p.loc[p[\"go_live_week\"].notna(), \"wave\"].unique())\n    xs = []\n    for w in waves:\n        col = f\"treated_w{w}\"\n        p[col] = ((p[\"wave\"] == w) & (p[\"treated\"] == 1)).astype(int)\n        xs.append(col)\n    beta, se = _fit(p, outcome, xs)\n    return {str(int(w)): {\"estimate\": float(b), \"se\": float(s)} for w, b, s in zip(waves, beta, se)}\n\"\"\"Store x week analysis panel from the warehouse.\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport sqlite3\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport numpy as np\nimport pandas as pd\n\n\ndef connect(db: Path) -> sqlite3.Connection:\n    return sqlite3.connect(f\"file:{Path(db).resolve()}?mode=ro\", uri=True)\n\n\ndef build(db: Path) -> pd.DataFrame:\n    con = connect(db)\n    try:\n        kpi = pd.read_sql_query(\"SELECT store_id, week_start, net_sales, customer_txns FROM kpi_store_week\", con)\n        plan = pd.read_sql_query(\"SELECT store_id, wave, planned_go_live FROM rollout_plan\", con)\n    finally:\n        con.close()\n    p = kpi.merge(plan, on=\"store_id\", how=\"left\")\n    last_week = p[\"week_start\"].max()\n    live = p[\"planned_go_live\"] <= last_week\n    p[\"go_live_week\"] = p[\"planned_go_live\"].where(live)\n    weeks = (pd.to_datetime(p[\"week_start\"]) - pd.to_datetime(p[\"go_live_week\"])).dt.days // 7\n    p[\"event_week\"] = weeks.astype(\"Int64\")\n    p[\"comparable\"] = (p[\"customer_txns\"] > 0).astype(int)\n    p[\"log_net_sales\"] = np.log(p[\"net_sales\"])\n    p[\"log_basket\"] = np.log(p[\"net_sales\"] / p[\"customer_txns\"])\n    p[\"treated\"] = (p[\"event_week\"].fillna(-1) >= 0).astype(int)\n    return p.sort_values([\"store_id\", \"week_start\"]).reset_index(drop=True)\n\"\"\"Readout files (docs/outputs/readout_contract.md).\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport json\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pandas as pd\n\nHURDLE = 0.025          # continuation hurdle, business case section 3\nPANEL_COLS = [\"store_id\", \"week_start\", \"wave\", \"go_live_week\", \"event_week\", \"comparable\", \"log_net_sales\"]\n\n\ndef _ci(e: dict) -> dict:\n    return {\"estimate\": e[\"estimate\"], \"ci_low\": e[\"estimate\"] - {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01UW5KK9WdGwYKBpQFuP4QQS","type":"tool_result","content":"# sco_readout release notes\n\n## 2.3.1 (2026-08-18)\n- `gate` writes `analysis_panel.csv` and `readout.json` in the layout Finance asked for\n  (`docs/outputs/readout_contract.md`).\n\n## 2.3.0 (2026-06-02)\n- Wave-level readout: one treatment indicator per wave in the fixed-effects regression.\n\n## 2.0.0 (2025-11-20)\n- Generalised from the ESL readout: store and week fixed effects, store-clustered standard errors, basket size as the\n  programme KPI.\n# Store KPI handbook (extract)\n\nOwner: Retail Finance. All store KPIs are reported in trading weeks that run **Monday to Sunday**; a week is labelled by\nits Monday (`week_start`).\n\n| KPI | Definition | Source |\n|---|---|---|\n| Net sales | merchandise sales net of returns and promotional markdowns, excluding VAT, lottery and the pharmacy counter | `kpi_store_week.net_sales` |\n| Customer transactions | completed checkout transactions (staffed lanes and self-checkout) | `kpi_store_week.customer_txns` |\n| Basket size | net sales / customer transactions | derived |\n| SCO share | share of customer transactions completed at self-checkout | `kpi_store_week.sco_txn_share` |\n| Pharmacy sales | pharmacy counter sales, reported separately (stores with a pharmacy only) | `kpi_store_week.pharmacy_sales` |\n\n## Comparable trading weeks\n\nA **comparable trading week** is a week in which the store traded its full hours on all seven days. A store-week with\nany record in `store_closures` (install works, weather, refrigeration, power, flooring) is not a comparable trading\nweek. Like-for-like reporting and programme evaluations use comparable trading weeks only; partial weeks are kept in the\nledger for completeness.\n\n## Notes\n\n- Transactions and basket size move in opposite directions when shoppers consolidate trips; net sales is the figure\n  the P&L uses.\n# Finance glossary (Store Investments, extract)\n\n**Uplift.** The change a programme causes in a store's figure: actual, minus what the store would have done over the\nsame weeks without the programme. For sales figures, uplift is expressed in log points (0.025 ≈ 2.5%).\n\n**Run-rate.** Performance once a change has bedded in: weeks 13 to 26 after go-live, counting the go-live week as\nweek 1. Weeks that are not comparable trading weeks (`docs/kpi_handbook.md`) are left out.\n\n**Store-level vs programme-level figures.** A store's run-rate uplift is the average over its run-rate weeks. A\nprogramme-level or wave-level figure is the simple average across the stores concerned (each store counts once,\nwhatever its size), because capital is committed per store.\n\n**Go-live.** The first trading week in which the installed equipment is in customer use.\n\n**Tranche.** A tranche of a staged programme is a set of waves released together.\n# SCO 2.0 business case (approved 2024-11-26, Capital Committee)\n\nSponsor: COO. Finance partner: FP&A (Store Investments).\n\n## 1. What we are buying\n\nSCO 2.0 replaces the self-checkout bank with the new scale-integrated units and, where the building allows it, a\nbig-basket self-checkout lane. Installation is staged in six waves (plan `rollout_plan`, version 2024-11).\n\n| Kit | Capex per store | Maintenance per year |\n|---|---|---|\n| Full (with big-basket lane) | £410k | £22k |\n| Compact | £265k | £15k |\n\n## 2. Why\n\nStore Operations expects faster checkout and larger consolidated shops. The Programme team tracks basket size and SCO\nshare as its programme KPIs.\n\n## 3. Staged capital release and continuation gate\n\nCapital is released in two tranches.\n\n- **Tranche 1 (waves 1–4)** was released at approval.\n- **Tranche 2 (waves 5–6)** is released only if the continuation gate is met: the expected **run-rate uplift in\n  weekly net sales for the stores in waves 5–6, as planned**, is at least **2.5%**. At 2.5% the tranche pays back\n  inside the kit's depreciation life at the planned kit mix; below it, it does not.\n\nThe gate figure is prepared by FP&A from the waves already live and presented to the Capital Committee with its\nuncertainty. Definitions follow the finance glossary (`docs/finance/glossary.md`).\n\n## 4. Out of scope\n\nReverting stores already installed is not considered (the capex is sunk and the kits have no resale value).\n# SCO 2.0 wave sequencing (Store Operations, November 2024)\n\nHow the store list was split into waves for plan version 2024-11.\n\n1. **Readiness first.** Waves 1–2 are weighted towards Supercentres: they have the floor space, the longest staffed\n   queues and dedicated install crews in every region.\n2. **Within a format, stores with a usable rear bagging bay go earlier.** The big-basket lane is the headline feature\n   and those installs are the ones the vendor wanted to prove first; stores without a bay were pushed to later waves.\n3. **Crew geography.** Within those groups, stores were allocated to waves by installer region so that a crew works\n   through neighbouring stores in sequence.\n4. Waves 5–6 hold the remaining stores.\n\nNo store was chosen or deferred because of its sales performance.\n# SCO 2.0 programme brief\n\nOwner: Store Transformation (Programme team). pd.to_timedelta(d.dt.dayofweek, unit=\"D\")).dt.strftime(\"%Y-%m-%d\")\n\n\ndef build(db: Path) -> pd.DataFrame:\n    con = connect(db)\n    try:\n        kpi = pd.read_sql_query(\"SELECT store_id, week_start, net_sales, customer_txns FROM kpi_store_week\", con)\n        plan = pd.read_sql_query(\"SELECT store_id, wave, planned_go_live, planned_kit FROM rollout_plan\", con)\n        stores = pd.read_sql_query(\"SELECT store_id, format FROM stores\", con)\n        go_live = pd.read_sql_query(\"SELECT store_id, event_date FROM install_log WHERE event = 'go_live'\", con)\n        closures = pd.read_sql_query(\"SELECT store_id, closure_date FROM store_closures\", con)\n    finally:\n        con.close()\n\n    p = kpi.merge(plan, on=\"store_id\", how=\"left\").merge(stores, on=\"store_id\", how=\"left\")\n    p[\"week_start\"] = _monday(p[\"week_start\"])\n    last_week = p[\"week_start\"].max()\n\n    # Go-live is what actually happened (install log), not the plan: the first week the kit is in customer use.\n    go_live[\"go_live_week\"] = _monday(go_live[\"event_date\"])\n    gl = go_live.groupby(\"store_id\", as_index=False)[\"go_live_week\"].min()\n    gl = gl[gl[\"go_live_week\"] <= last_week]\n    p = p.merge(gl, on=\"store_id\", how=\"left\")\n    weeks = (pd.to_datetime(p[\"week_start\"]) - pd.to_datetime(p[\"go_live_week\"])).dt.days // 7\n    p[\"event_week\"] = weeks.astype(\"Int64\")\n\n    # Comparable trading week: no closure record of any kind in the store's Monday-Sunday week.\n    closures[\"week_start\"] = _monday(closures[\"closure_date\"])\n    closed = closures[[\"store_id\", \"week_start\"]].drop_duplicates().assign(_closed=1)\n    p = p.merge(closed, on=[\"store_id\", \"week_start\"], how=\"left\")\n    p[\"comparable\"] = p[\"_closed\"].isna().astype(int)\n\n    p[\"log_net_sales\"] = np.log(p[\"net_sales\"])\n    p[\"log_basket\"] = np.log(p[\"net_sales\"] / p[\"customer_txns\"])\n    p[\"treated\"] = (p[\"event_week\"].fillna(-1) >= 0).astype(int)\n    return p.drop(columns=\"_closed\").sort_values([\"store_id\", \"week_start\"]).reset_index(drop=True)\nEOF"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1255,"cache_read_input_tokens":35647,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":1255,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0},"output_tokens":8,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"global"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"bcd77d6f-9f50-465f-9dfe-f7dc2173aaa7","uuid":"9db7c9f6-a914-407c-b61c-b726e4b81cb2","timestamp":"2026-10-01T01:30:20.692Z","request_id":"req_011CfaeinVQe4ibua6gmZ9H4"}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CfaemkGnN8UhMuWxZpecv","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_018xy1wgTwKXgGvRn3F3EJU7","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"cd /workspace; python - <<'EOF'\nsrc=open('sco_readout/estimate.py').read()\nsrc=src.replace('\"\"\"Panel regression with store and week fixed effects (house method since the ESL readout).\"\"\"',\n'''\"\"\"Programme effect estimators.\n\n`run_rate_readout` is the gate method. `twfe` / `twfe_by_wave` are the 2.x pooled regressions, kept for the old\nbasket-size readouts only: on a staggered rollout they compare later-treated stores with already-treated ones and\naverage every post-go-live week, so they do not estimate the run-rate uplift.\n\"\"\"''')\nopen('sco_readout/estimate.py','w').write(src)\nEOF\ncat >> sco_readout/estimate.py <<'EOF'\n\n\n# --- Run-rate uplift by imputation ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n#\n# Counterfactual for each store-week: store effect + format-by-week effect, fitted only on untreated comparable weeks\n# (stores not yet live, and live stores before go-live less an anticipation window covering prewire and install).\n# Uplift = actual - counterfactual on run-rate weeks; averaged per store, then across stores (each store counts once).\n# Intervals: store bootstrap stratified by wave, re-fitting the counterfactual in every replicate.\n\nRUN_RATE = (12, 25)       # weeks 13-26 after go-live, go-live week = week 1 (finance glossary)\nANTICIPATION = 3          # pre-go-live weeks left out of the counterfactual fit (prewire 2-3 weeks before go-live)\nN_BOOT = 999\nSEED = 20241126           # business case approval date; fixed so reruns are identical\n\n\ndef _solve_fe(store: np.ndarray, cell: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray, w: np.ndarray, n_s: int, n_c: int):\n    \"\"\"Weighted least squares y ~ store + cell effects; returns (a, b) with NaN for unidentified levels.\"\"\"\n    ws = np.bincount(store, weights=w, minlength=n_s)\n    wc = np.bincount(cell, weights=w, minlength=n_c)\n    rs = np.bincount(store, weights=w * y, minlength=n_s)\n    rc = np.bincount(cell, weights=w * y, minlength=n_c)\n    N = np.bincount(store * n_c + cell, weights=w, minlength=n_s * n_c).reshape(n_s, n_c)\n    inv_ws = np.divide(1.0, ws, out=np.zeros(n_s), where=ws > 0)\n    S = np.diag(wc) - N.T @ (N * inv_ws[:, None])\n    b = np.linalg.lstsq(S, rc - N.T @ (rs * inv_ws), rcond=None)[0]\n    a = (rs - N @ b) * inv_ws\n    a[ws == 0] = np.nan\n    b[wc == 0] = np.nan\n    return a, b\n\n\nclass _Design:\n    def __init__(self, panel: pd.DataFrame, outcome: str):\n        p = panel\n        self.store_ids, store = np.unique(p[\"store_id\"].to_numpy(), return_inverse=True)\n        _, cell = np.unique((p[\"format\"].astype(str) + \"|\" + p[\"week_start\"]).to_numpy(), return_inverse=True)\n        self.n_s, self.n_c = len(self.store_ids), int(cell.max()) + 1\n        ew = p[\"event_week\"].astype(\"float\").to_numpy()\n        comparable = p[\"comparable\"].to_numpy() == 1\n        y = p[outcome].to_numpy(float)\n        fit = comparable & (np.isnan(ew) | (ew < -ANTICIPATION))\n        rr = comparable & (ew >= RUN_RATE[0]) & (ew <= RUN_RATE[1])\n        self.fit = (store[fit], cell[fit], y[fit])\n        self.rr = (store[rr], cell[rr], y[rr])\n\n        per_store = p.groupby(\"store_id\").agg(\n            wave=(\"wave\", \"first\"), live=(\"go_live_week\", lambda s: s.notna().any()),\n            kit=(\"kit\", \"first\")).reindex(self.store_ids)\n        self.wave = per_store[\"wave\"].to_numpy()\n        self.live = per_store[\"live\"].to_numpy(bool)\n        self.kit = per_store[\"kit\"].to_numpy()\n\n    def store_uplift(self, w_store: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:\n        s, c, y = self.fit\n        a, b = _solve_fe(s, c, y, w_store[s], self.n_s, self.n_c)\n        s, c, y = self.rr\n        tau = y - a[s] - b[c]\n        ok = ~np.isnan(tau)\n        n = np.bincount(s[ok], minlength=self.n_s)\n        tot = np.bincount(s[ok], weights=tau[ok], minlength=self.n_s)\n        return np.divide(tot, n, out=np.full(self.n_s, np.nan), where=n > 0)\n\n\ndef _mean(x: np.ndarray, w: np.ndarray) -> float:\n    ok = ~np.isnan(x) & (w > 0)\n    return float(np.sum(x[ok] * w[ok]) / np.sum(w[ok])) if ok.any() else float(\"nan\")\n\n\ndef _figures(d: _Design, w: np.ndarray, waves, target: np.ndarray, kits) -> np.ndarray:\n    \"\"\"[wave figures..., gate figure] for store weights w (bootstrap multiplicities).\"\"\"\n    u = d.store_uplift(w)\n    out = [_mean(u, w * (d.live & (d.wave == wv))) for wv in waves]\n    # Gate: the target stores' expected uplift, predicting each from the live stores with the same kit.\n    by_kit = {k: _mean(u, w * (d.live & (d.kit == k))) for k in kits}\n    out.append(_mean(np.array([by_kit[k] for k in d.kit[target]]), np.ones(target.sum())))\n    return np.array(out)\n\n\ndef run_rate_readout(panel: pd.DataFrame, outcome: str = \"log_net_sales\") -> tuple[dict, dict, dict]:\n    \"\"\"Wave-level run-rate uplifts, the continuation-gate figure and kit-level diagnostics, each with a 95% interval.\n\n    Gate target: stores in planned waves with no store live in the extract (the waves awaiting release), at their\n    planned kit.\n    \"\"\"\n    d = _Design(panel, outcome)\n    waves = sorted(set(d.wave[d.live]))\n    target = np.isin(d.wave, waves, invert=True)\n    if not target.any():\n        raise ValueError(\"no planned waves are still awaiting go-live: there is no gate population\")\n    kits = sorted(set(d.kit[target]))\n    missing = [k for k in kits if not (d.live & (d.kit == k)).any()]\n    if missing:\n        raise ValueError(f\"no live stores with kit {missing}: their uplift cannot be estimated from the waves live\")\n\n    point = _figures(d, np.ones(d.n_s), waves, target, kits)\n    rng = np.random.default_rng(SEED)\n    strata = [np.flatnonzero(d.wave == wv) for wv in sorted(set(d.wave))]\n    boot = np.empty((N_BOOT, len(point)))\n    for i in range(N_BOOT):\n        w = np.zeros(d.n_s)\n        for idx in strata:\n            np.add.at(w, rng.choice(idx, size=len(idx), replace=True), 1.0)\n python - <<'EOF'\nf='RELEASES.md';s=open(f).read()\ns=s.replace('# sco_readout release notes\\n','''# sco_readout release notes\n\n## 2.4.0 (2026-10-01)\n- `gate` now estimates the continuation-gate figure as defined in the business case (§3) and finance glossary:\n  - outcome is log weekly **net sales** (was basket size);\n  - go-live from `install_log` (was the plan, which is not updated when stores slip);\n  - comparable trading weeks exclude any store-week with a `store_closures` record, on Monday-Sunday weeks\n    (was \"any transactions\");\n  - **run-rate** uplift: weeks 13-26 after go-live, per store, then a simple average across stores\n    (was a pooled average of all post-go-live weeks);\n  - counterfactual imputed from store and format-by-week effects fitted on untreated weeks only (not-yet-live\n    stores, pre-go-live weeks less a 3-week prewire/install window), replacing the pooled two-way regression,\n    which is biased on a staggered rollout and showed clear pre-trends;\n  - gate population: stores in planned waves not yet live, each predicted from live stores with the same kit;\n  - 95% intervals from a wave-stratified store bootstrap (999 replicates, fixed seed).\n''')\nopen(f,'w').write(s)\nfor f in ['sco_readout/__init__.py']:\n    s=open(f).read().replace('2.3.1','2.4.0');open(f,'w').write(s)\nEOF\nrm -rf /tmp/x/out2"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1261,"cache_read_input_tokens":51675,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":1261,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0},"output_tokens":8,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"global"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"bcd77d6f-9f50-465f-9dfe-f7dc2173aaa7","uuid":"31662ada-c9bc-4a2e-8c3c-f01c35bce892","timestamp":"2026-10-01T01:37:01.532Z","request_id":"req_011CfafGUkSu86Y2yjqP4zUa"}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CfafHHmSCL1s82wVjr15V","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"# SCO 2.0 tranche 2: gate figure and recommendation\n\n**Recommendation: don't release tranche 2 as planned.** The gate figure is **+1.1% (95% interval +1.0% to +1.2%)**, against a 2.5% hurdle. `readout.json` gives the decision as `stop`.\n\n| | Run-rate net sales uplift (95% interval) |\n|---|---|\n| Wave 1 | +4.1% (+3.7 to +4.4) |\n| Wave 2 | +3.5% (+3.1 to +3.8) |\n| Wave 3 | +3.1% (+2.8 to +3.6) |\n| Wave 4 | +1.9% (+1.5 to +2.3) |\n| **Gate (waves 5–6 as planned, 364 stores)** | **+1.1% (+1.0 to +1.2)** |\n\n**What drives it is the kit.** Stores with the full kit (with the big-basket lane) gain about +4.3% in every format. Stores with the compact kit gain about 0%: −0.4% in Neighbourhood and −0.1% in Market. The waves get weaker from 1 to 4 because each one has more compact stores. Waves 5–6 are 71% compact by plan, which pulls the gate figure well below the hurdle. This also matches what Store Operations are hearing: shoppers like the units but aren't spending more.\n\nAn option the Committee could look at, though I haven't costed it: release only the full-kit stores in waves 5–6. Those are about +4.3%, above the hurdle.\n\n## Why the earlier figures shouldn't go to the Committee\n- **Programme readout (+5.5%) and FP&A notebook (~+6.7%):** both use the old pooled regression. It compares later stores with ones already live, takes go-live dates from the plan (about a quarter of stores went live 1–4 weeks late), and averages every week after go-live instead of weeks 13–26. It also counts weeks with closures as normal trading weeks.\n- **Upward trend before go-live:** the early waves are mostly Supercentres, which were already growing faster than the comparison stores before anything was installed. That trend gets counted as uplift. Comparing each store only with stores of the same format removes it.\n- **Programme readout only:** it measures basket size, not net sales. Bigger baskets can come with fewer visits, so a basket increase doesn't mean more sales.\n- **Both:** neither figure is for the waves 5–6 stores. They describe the stores already live, which are mostly full-kit.\n\n## How it's estimated (for when the Committee asks)\n1. For each store and week, estimate what sales would have been without SCO 2.0. This comes from the store's own level plus a week-by-week trend for its format. That trend is fitted only on weeks before the store was affected: stores not yet live, and live stores' weeks up to 3 weeks before go-live, to leave out the prewire and install period. Only normal trading weeks are used.\n2. Uplift is actual minus that estimate, averaged over weeks 13–26 for each store. Wave figures are then a simple average across stores, so each store counts once.\n3. The gate figure predicts each waves 5–6 store from live stores with the same planned kit, then averages.\n4. Intervals come from resampling stores within each wave, 999 times with a fixed seed.\n\nThe weeks before go-live show no trend under this method. The kit-level results barely change if I leave out 0 or 8 weeks before go-live instead of 3, or add region-by-week trends.\n\n**One assumption I couldn't test:** the business case assumes sister stores are at least six miles apart, so live stores aren't taking sales from Meridian stores not yet live. The extract has no location data to check this. If it is happening, the true figure would be lower still.\n\n## Requirements\n1. **Command and outputs:** the command writes both files to the contract, with one panel row for each of the 140,400 rows in `kpi_store_week`.\n2. **Works on other extracts:** nothing is tied to particular stores, waves, formats, dates or values in this one. The gate population is \"planned waves with no store live yet\", which is waves 5–6 here.\n3. **System of record:** the warehouse wasn't modified, and no outputs or reports were hand-edited. The Programme readout and FP&A notebook are unchanged, and the notebook still runs the old method.\n4. **Reruns and run time:** two runs gave byte-identical files, and a run takes about 46 seconds.\n5. **Regenerated outputs:** `out/` now holds the regenerated `analysis_panel.csv` and `readout.json` for this extract.\n\nI rewrote `sco_readout/panel.py`, `estimate.py`, `cli.py` and `report.py`, bumped the package to 2.4.0, and noted the method changes in `RELEASES.md`."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":738,"cache_read_input_tokens":52936,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":738,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0},"output_tokens":8,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"global"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"bcd77d6f-9f50-465f-9dfe-f7dc2173aaa7","uuid":"0e5e1682-bfc6-44d7-9896-d4a2a0032057","timestamp":"2026-10-01T01:37:20.324Z","request_id":"req_011CfafHH5W7VuiCB86jUn57"}
